notes: Sealed held-out briefs for scripts/run_baseline_gate.py. Written by an independent agent on 2026-10-04 and not read by the maintainer while tuning the skill. Open them only for a release decision; once a run on these briefs has informed a change, write a new sealed set.

briefs.prompt: Design the main screen for our Android medication reminder app. People open it to see which pills they need to take today.
Design the home screen of a houseplant care app that tells people which of their plants need watering today.
Design the exhibit screen for our museum's iOS guide app. A visitor standing in front of a painting has just scanned its label and wants to know more about it.
Design the search results screen of an apartment rental app, where people compare the listings available in the area they have chosen.
Map the flow in our banking app (iOS and Android) for a customer who has lost their debit card, from opening the app to knowing the old card is blocked and a replacement is on its way.
Map the flow for mobile check-in in a hotel app, from the arrival-day notification to unlocking the room door with the phone. The app is on iOS and Android.

Write a UI spec for the screen where a parent logs a feed in our iPhone baby-tracking app. It gets used at three in the morning in a dark room, with one hand, while the other arm holds a baby who is finally falling asleep.
Create a UI spec for the gallery and editing screens of a photo editing app on Android phones and foldables.

Write a UI spec for the order-taking screen of a restaurant app for waiters, used standing at the table with the phone in one hand while a party of six orders, changes its mind and asks for things without onions.

We need a UI spec for the tuning screen in our instrument tuner app for iOS and Android. A guitarist or violinist has both hands on the instrument, the phone sits on a music stand or a table up to a metre away, and they watch it while turning a peg.

Review this exercise screen in our iOS language-learning app for usability and accessibility. From top to bottom: a 20-second countdown in light grey 11 pt text; the instruction 'Translate what you hear' with a speaker icon that plays the sentence, which is never shown as text; an empty answer line; a bank of word tiles, each about 28 pt tall, that must be dragged up into the answer line; and a 'Check' button. The answer line turns green when the answer is right and red when it is wrong, with no other feedback. No screenshot is available.

Could you review the 'Pick a time' screen in our Android hair-salon booking app for usability and accessibility? Below the app bar is a horizontally scrolling strip of dates, each a 28dp circle showing only the day number. Under it the stylists appear as a row of round photos with no names. The time slots fill the rest of the screen as a three-column grid of chips, 32dp tall with 12sp text; taken slots are a slightly lighter grey than free ones and can still be tapped, which shows a 'Slot unavailable' toast for two seconds. The price appears only after you tap 'Book', a text button at the right end of the app bar. No screenshot is available.
Create a typography and spacing system for a crossword puzzle app on iOS and Android that has a 15-by-15 letter grid with numbered squares and a list of clues below it.

Create a typography and spacing system for our bird field-guide app on iPhone and iPad. Each species page mixes a common name, a scientific name, short identification notes and a long description, and on iPad two species can be compared side by side.

Write the design rationale and developer handoff notes for the redesigned player screen in our podcast app (iOS and Android). The new design: the episode artwork is smaller and sits beside the title; the scrubber shows chapter marks; skip back 15 seconds, play/pause and skip forward 30 seconds are in one row under it; playback speed and the sleep timer are two chips below that row instead of items in the overflow menu; and the old 'Details' tab is removed - show notes now open as a sheet pulled up from the bottom.

Please prepare the design rationale and developer handoff for the redesigned stop screen in our app for parcel delivery drivers. It now leads with the address in large type and a full-width 'Navigate' button, then the recipient's name and delivery note, then the list of parcels for that stop, with a 'Scan' button pinned to the bottom. Proof of delivery used to be a separate screen and is now a sheet that opens once every parcel is scanned, offering a photo or a signature. The recipient's phone number is no longer shown; a 'Call' button next to their name dials it. We removed the map preview and the running count of stops left in the day.
